title: snRNA-Seq
scope: Lacar 2016 single-nucleus RNA-seq implementation associated with this Illumina entry, at the depicted nuclei-isolation-to-indexed-library level. The drawn individually sorted-nucleus route is represented using the primary-supported plate Smart-seq2 preparation for novel-environment nuclei. The home-cage C1 preparation is contextual, not an additional depicted branch or a sequential capture step. The label does not assert equivalence of all snRNA-seq assays.

operations.label: Lyse and centrifuge

operations.information_effect: The continuing material represents the nuclear compartment rather than the complete cellular RNA pool.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven blocks apply at the declared schematic scope to the Lacar sorted-well nuclear preparation: lysis/centrifugation, sorting, first-strand synthesis, template-switch-associated cDNA synthesis, transcriptome PCR, tagmentation, and gap repair/library PCR. The left Single cell/RNA/poly(A) drawings explain the analyte; they do not show a separately isolated RNA product being returned to a cell suspension. Nuclei and supernatant are explicit centrifugation outputs; only nuclei continue. The three snRNA-Seq rows show one shared drawn route, not alternative branches to pool. Adjacent Smart-Seq2, FRISCR, NanoCAGE/CAGEscan and standalone LNA/dimethyl-sulfate drawings are outside the assigned target. Poster references resolve to Grindberg 2013, whereas the card explicitly identifies Lacar 2016; the shared schematic does not establish identical complete protocols. The candidate collection page has the snRNA-Seq heading and Lacar reference but its extracted text includes LNA/template-switch labels, whereas the supplied snRNA-Seq row does not label an LNA modification. It is secondary catalogue evidence and is not used to import that modification into this row.

corrections.diagram_observation: The row depicts Sort nuclei → Nucleus → First strand synthesis. The associated catalogue says nuclei are sorted into individual wells and then states that individual nuclei are amplified using microfluidics-assisted capture/reaction machinery, which can be read as a single sequential preparation.
corrections.primary_statement: Lacar separates home-cage NEUN+PROX1+ nuclei processed on Fluidigm C1 from novel-environment (NE) nuclei processed with plate-based Smart-seq2. The actual graph uses the depicted sorted-well route, supported for NE nuclei, and does not append C1 capture to that route. Smart-seq2 here is an embedded amplification protocol, not another target method.
